{
  "hook": "While Sauvignon Blanc dominates the region, this bottle leverages cool nights to maintain sharp acidity. Consistent production across vintages keeps the profile stable despite weather variations.",
  "wine_summary": "Produced at scale by Constellation Brands, this label prioritizes consistency over vintage variation. The wine reflects Marlborough\u2019s alluvial plains rather than specific hillside sites, resulting in a straightforward fruit profile. Buyers get a reliable expression of New Zealand Chardonnay without site-specific complexity.",
  "terroir_expression": "Gravelly loam soils deposited by ancient river beds drain water quickly and stress the vines. High sunshine hours in the Wairau Valley ripen the fruit, while cool maritime breezes from the Pacific Ocean preserve natural acidity. This climate combination yields green apple and citrus notes rather than tropical heaviness.",
  "vinification_summary": "During fermentation, stainless steel tanks protect primary fruit aromas from oxidation. The winemaking team limits new oak usage, avoiding the vanilla and toast flavors found in barrel-aged counterparts. Malolactic fermentation may be partially applied to soften the sharp malic acid into creamier lactic acid without adding heavy butter notes.",
  "food_pairing": "Serve shrimp scampi with lemon butter sauce so acidity cuts through the fat. Roast chicken with thyme matches the subtle stone fruit notes without overwhelming the palate. Nashville hot chicken works because the cool fruit tempers the spice heat. Grilled halibut with salsa verde aligns with the herbal undertones. Vegetable risotto benefits from the wine\u2019s clean finish against the creamy starch.",
  "comparable_wines": "Buyers seeking similar Marlborough origin should consider Kim Crawford Chardonnay for comparable price. Villa Maria Private Bin Chardonnay offers slightly more texture at comparable cost. Santa Margherita Pinot Grigio provides a different grape but similar crisp, clean profile for the same audience.",
  "style_profile": "Light-bodied dry white with high acidity and citrus focus",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Freshness remains intact only if consumed immediately. Store upright in a cool cupboard away from direct sunlight.",
  "value_assessment": "$15 to $18 places this bottle against Kim Crawford and Stoneleigh on retail shelves. The cost reflects large-scale production efficiency rather than vineyard specificity. It delivers consistent quality for the price but lacks the depth of single-vineyard options.",
  "market_position": "Restaurants list this as a safe by-the-glass option for customers unfamiliar with New Zealand whites. Grocery stores stock it prominently alongside Sauvignon Blanc for everyday drinkers. Collectors ignore this label in favor of small-production growers.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this bottle if you seek mineral drive or oak complexity. Choose it when consistency matters more than character. The tradeoff is simplicity in exchange for availability and price stability.",
  "aging_potential_years": 0,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 1,
